summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for shortness of breath, cough, and orthopnea. Evaluation revealed mild fluid overload with elevated BNP and radiographic evidence of interstitial pulmonary edema, consistent with a heart failure exacerbation. He also had symptoms of acute bronchitis, for which he was treated with azithromycin, albuterol, and cough suppressants. His condition improved with oral furosemide and supportive care. Electrolytes and renal function remained stable, and cardiac enzymes were negative. Smoking cessation support was provided with a nicotine patch. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue antibiotics, monitor daily weight, and follow up with cardiology.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
